title: Finite product transport of scalar action diagrams
statement: Let C and D be categories with finite products [def-weil-category-product], L : C -> D a functor preserving finite limits, RV and AV objects of C, RU and AU objects of D, and er : RU ~= L(RV), ea : AU ~= L(AV) isomorphisms. Let mulV : RV x RV -> RV, mulU : RU x RU -> RU, oneV : 1_C -> RV, oneU : 1_D -> RU, and muV : RV x AV -> AV be morphisms. Write c(X,Y) : L(X x Y) -> L(X) x L(Y) for the canonical product comparison. Assume L(mulV) = c(RV,RV);(er^-1 x er^-1);mulU;er and L(oneV) = !;oneU;er, where semicolon denotes composition from left to right. Assume the source associativity equation (mulV x id);muV = <pr1;pr1, <pr1;pr2,pr2>;muV>;muV and unit equation <!;oneV,id>;muV = id. Define mu = (er x ea);c(RV,AV)^-1;L(muV);ea^-1. Then (mulU x id);mu = <pr1;pr1, <pr1;pr2,pr2>;mu>;mu and <!;oneU,id>;mu = id. No monoid laws for mulV itself and no additive structure are assumed.

source.place: Tag 03D2, proof of lemma-pullback-module; Associativity and unit transport of the scalar action, inverse-image module construction

proof.text: Set k = (er x ea);c(RV,AV)^-1. Its composites with L(pr1) and L(pr2) are pr1;er and pr2;ea. For arbitrary maps a,b and t into an image L(T), equality of these two projections shows <a,b>;k = t;L(<f,g>) whenever a;er=t;L(f) and b;ea=t;L(g).

Use the double scalar comparison er2 = (er x er);c(RV,RV)^-1 and the triple comparison t = (er2 x ea);c(RV x RV,AV)^-1. The multiplication transport equation identifies the first composite with mulU;er. Apply the preceding pairing identity to the multiplied-scalar and nested-action maps. Apply L to the source associativity equation and cancel ea to obtain target associativity.

Apply the pairing identity with t=ea to the unit insertion. The one transport equation and uniqueness of maps to the terminal object identify the scalar projection; the other projection is ea. Apply L to the source unit equation and cancel ea to obtain target unit.

lean.statement:
theorem transportScalarActionDiagrams
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [HasFiniteProducts C]
    {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [HasFiniteProducts D]
    (L : C ⥤ D) [PreservesFiniteLimits L]
    (RV AV : C) (RU AU : D) (er : RU ≅ L.obj RV) (ea : AU ≅ L.obj AV)
    (mulV : RV ⨯ RV ⟶ RV) (mulU : RU ⨯ RU ⟶ RU)
    (oneV : ⊤_ C ⟶ RV) (oneU : ⊤_ D ⟶ RU) (muV : RV ⨯ AV ⟶ AV)
    (hMul : L.map mulV = prodComparison L RV RV ≫
      prod.map er.inv er.inv ≫ mulU ≫ er.hom)
    (hOne : L.map oneV = terminal.from _ ≫ oneU ≫ er.hom)
    (hAssoc : prod.map mulV (𝟙 AV) ≫ muV =
      prod.lift (prod.fst ≫ prod.fst)
        (prod.lift (prod.fst ≫ prod.snd) prod.snd ≫ muV) ≫ muV)
    (hUnit : prod.lift (terminal.from AV ≫ oneV) (𝟙 AV) ≫ muV = 𝟙 AV) :
    let mu := prod.map er.hom ea.hom ≫ inv (prodComparison L RV AV) ≫
      L.map muV ≫ ea.inv
    (prod.map mulU (𝟙 AU) ≫ mu =
      prod.lift (prod.fst ≫ prod.fst)
        (prod.lift (prod.fst ≫ prod.snd) prod.snd ≫ mu) ≫ mu) ∧
    (prod.lift (terminal.from AU ≫ oneU) (𝟙 AU) ≫ mu = 𝟙 AU)
